claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the vehicle covered 27.69 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 21.3 km, an excess of 6.39 km. That excess is 30.0% of the optimal distance, above the 20% establishment threshold, and 6.39 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km establishment threshold. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The governing figure is the trace distance, not the rounded 27.7 km convenience copy on the trip record, exactly as POL-RD-01 requires.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02858 and the same pickup/start timestamp of 2026-08-23T08:41:14+08:00, so limb (a) is satisfied. Limb (b) is satisfied by the 6.39 km / 30.0% excess measured from an unimpaired trace (100.0% coverage, 218 fixes, 10 s sampling, zero gaps, max gap 0 s). The burden therefore shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause, and no such artifact exists on this record.

The driver's only explanation is 'Followed navigation.' That is a general assertion of a traffic or routing cause, and POL-RD-08 provides that a general assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge the driver's burden. No traffic_advisory is on file for this trip: the sole advisory artifact is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and the excuse carries no weight. Under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. The chat log for this trip contains zero messages, so there is no rider instruction meeting POL-RD-04(a) to (c), no waypoint_hint to test against the 200 m corroboration radius, and no road named. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

No relocation clause rescues the driver either. The trip_record shows original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. POL-RD-05 therefore cannot be run and the booked optimal of 21.3 km stands as the baseline.

The trip is not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 does not apply: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. The matched-itinerary baseline that clause substitutes for the solo optimal is simply not in play here, and the 21.3 km booked optimal is the correct comparator.
The fare model is METERED, not UPFRONT_QUOTE, and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not close off the distance-and-time refund. POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and the refund is arithmetic.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs on the booked optimal route: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 21.3 + 0.28 x 28.8) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = SGD 28.6390. Charged_total is SGD 35.52. Refund = 35.52 - 28.6390 = SGD 6.8810, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, i.e. SGD 6.90. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share (it is 19.37% of charged_total), so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries it.

The rider is entitled to the refund on the distance and time lines because the deviation is established and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it. The rider filed this dispute, so a PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the contested amount to the filing party and leaves the rider not carrying the disputed portion of the charge.

No separate ERP or surcharge correction is due. The fare_breakdown carries zero ERP gantries, tolls_erp of 0.0, and an airport_surcharge of 0.0 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no off-route gantry and no phantom line to refund under POL-RD-09. The off-route ERP total is SGD 0.00 and is comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure in any event.

The driver's profile does not support a repeat-deviation uplift, and I do not claim one. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the POL-RD-06 threshold of 3, and 1/309 completed trips in 90 days is 0.0032, below the 0.05 ratio test. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is 1 but is a near-synonym trap and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure under POL-GEN-01. The rider's remedy is therefore the POL-RD-02 partial refund and nothing more.

The rider's own profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration add-on: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4, so no independent corroboration beyond the gps_trace is required for this claim. The rider's prior_disputes_filed and prior_disputes_upheld are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground no finding.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: it has zero gaps, a max_gap_sec of 0.0, a 10 s sampling interval against an expected 10 s, and 100.0% coverage across 218 fixes. No limb (a) to (c) fires, so no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The deviation is established on the trace alone.

The excess of 6.39 km is below the 8.0 km absolute materiality threshold and the 30.0% excess is below the 50% materiality threshold, so this is an established but not MATERIAL deviation. POL-RD-06's driver_profile check is not mandatory on materiality grounds, and no FULL_REFUND uplift is available. I do not overstate the case: the rider's remedy is the partial refund computed under POL-RD-02.

claims.text: The rider's claim is proven on the platform's own trace: the GPS polyline between the recorded pickup and dropoff events measures 27.69 km against a booked optimal of 21.3 km, an excess of 6.39 km. That excess is 30.0% of optimal, above the 20% establishment threshold, and 6.39 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km threshold. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The governing figure is the trace distance, not the rounded 27.7 km convenience copy on the trip record, exactly as POL-RD-01 requires.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 218 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds across the whole 36 minute trip. There is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained interval above 30 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met and the trace is not impaired for policy purposes. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'Followed navigation.' That is a general assertion, not a clause invocation: it names no traffic advisory, no rider instruction, no amended endpoint and no pooled itinerary. Under POL-RD-08 the burden shifted to the driver once the rider showed a threshold-meeting excess on an unimpaired trace, and a general assertion unsupported by an artifact ID discharges nothing. No exculpatory clause is engaged on this record.

The driver's traffic excuse is weightless on this record. The bundle holds no traffic advisory covering the Tampines Mall corridor in this window: EV-ADVIS-02858-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cites no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not triggered and the case does not escalate on that ground. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour can be run: the chat log for this trip carries zero messages, no first or last message timestamp, and no waypoint_hint. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log, timestamped before the vehicle leaves the optimal corridor or within 3 minutes after, and corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of the waypoint. With no chat log content at all, the clause is unavailable and no distance is excluded from the excess.

No relocation clause applies. The trip record shows original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. There was no pin move, no chat-supplied alternative address and no platform-directed bay assignment, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 21.3 km remains the baseline.

This is not a pooled trip. The trip record carries vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. POL-RD-12 does not apply, so no distance is excluded as co-rider collection or set-down and the matched-itinerary baseline is not in play.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and POL-RD-11 does not. The fare breakdown records fare_model METERED, quoted_fare_sgd null, surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare breakdown itself, and charged_total SGD 35.52. Recomputing on the booked optimal route: (3.80 + 0.75 x 21.3 + 0.28 x 28.8) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 28.6390. Refund = 35.52 - 28.6390 = 6.8810, rounded up to SGD 6.90. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.90.

No ERP or surcharge correction is due on top of the distance refund. The fare breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and a total of SGD 0.00, no airport surcharge, and no waiting time fee, so there is no off-route pass-through to refund under POL-RD-09(2) and no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge under POL-RD-09(4). The distance refund under POL-RD-02 already comprehends the pass-through lines and nothing may be added on top of it.

The repeat-deviation check does not fire against the driver, and I do not press it. The driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 309, a ratio of 0.0032, far below the 0.05 limb, and the count is below the 3-or-more limb. No pattern is established under POL-RD-06, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral follow from this trip. I note for completeness that prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim. deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a rider with 4 or more claims and 1 or fewer substantiated does not apply, and no extra corroboration beyond the trace is required. The rider's other profile fields are context only and ground no finding.

The rider has carried the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02858 and the trace runs from the recorded trip_started event at 08:41:14 to the trip_completed event at 09:17:24, matching the trip record's started_at and ended_at. The artifacts describe the same trip and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace, so the burden shifted to the driver and was not discharged.

The contested amount is SGD 9.00 and the computed refund is SGD 6.90, which is below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold, so the monetary effect is executable on issue subject to appeal. The refund is also far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total, so no POL-RD-10(6) escalation is engaged.

To both parties: the rider's claim is upheld in part.
